summary:
Lunar Outpost is a browser-based game that puts players in charge of a Moon base for six days. Each day, they split 20 supply units across four systems: Life Support, Radiation Shield, Power, and Food. There is no perfect answer and no room to max everything.
The twist: the game runs on real NASA data. Solar flares and coronal mass ejections pulled live from NASA's DONKI API set the radiation risk each day. Skip the shield and a real event hurts your crew. Starve the power grid and life support drops with it. Every trade-off has a consequence, and after each day the game explains exactly why things went the way they did.
The science facts between rounds come from NASA's Open Science Data Repository, real space biology research written plainly enough for a 7-year-old to follow.
No installation, no accounts, no build step. Open the file in a browser and play.
Built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, ages 7 to 12.
details:
Lunar Outpost: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer
NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026

What we built
A 6-day lunar base survival game for ages 7 to 12. Players manage four systems: Life Support, Radiation Shield, Power, and Food. Each day they get 20 supply units to split across all four. Every choice has a consequence.

How it works
The game fetches live solar flare and CME data from NASA DONKI. Real events set the radiation risk each day. A weak shield against a real X-class flare hurts the crew. Low power drags down life support and kills crop growth. After each day the game explains what happened and why.

Space biology facts from NASA OSDR appear between rounds, grounding the game in real research.

Tech
Vanilla HTML, CSS and JavaScript. No dependencies, no build step, no accounts. Opens in any browser.

Why it matters
Kids learn that every unit they give to one system is a unit taken from another. That is not a game rule. That is how real mission planning works.
